contract:
Static native scheduling reference for Meta/Core 0.9.4.
This is source documentation, not an observed destination catalog, tool grant,
installed schedule, invocation result or restart proof. Match the selected Meta
SDK first; separately verify the actual gateway and granted tool catalog.

Native authoring:
- The eight meerkat_schedule_* schemas below come from Core v0.9.4 tools.rs,
  including the CurrentSessionScheduleToolDispatcher current_session shortcut.
- Create requires trigger, target, misfire_policy, overlap_policy and
  missing_target_policy. Update is flat: schedule_id plus changed create fields.
  No submission idempotency key, revision precondition or desired_definition is
  advertised. Omitted update fields retain their values.
- Get, pause, resume, delete and occurrences take schedule_id; list takes {}.
  Pause stops future firing but does not cancel in-flight work. Delete is final.
- Host-runnable targets ARE advertised in 0.9.4:
  {"target_kind":"host_runnable","runnable":"published-name","params":{...}}.
  runnable is the name of an already registered host runnable; params is optional
  opaque JSON. This target has no type field. It does not register a runnable,
  grant tool access or establish permission to act. Register the runnable before
  restored schedules can fire and inspect the host's actual capabilities.
- Responsible members can use a session target with type=current_session and
  action={"type":"prompt","prompt":"..."}. This shortcut is resolved by the
  host before persistence; it is not a stored TargetBinding variant. Depending
  on host composition, readback can use a resumable session, a stable mob-member
  identity, or Meta's bridged mob-member send target. Read the returned target
  and check the intended owner rather than requiring literal shortcut equality.
  Do not fabricate host identities or route around native policy checks.

Native readback:
- Create/get/update/pause/resume/delete return a Schedule object directly.
  List returns {"schedules":[...]}; occurrences returns {"occurrences":[...]}.
- Schedule uses schedule_id, phase and revision, not id/status/version aliases.
  phase is active, paused or deleted. ScheduleConfig fields are flattened.
  Keep the returned trigger, resolved target, policies and exact native ID.
- commissioning_agent is native-owned and optional on readback. It is NOT a
  create/update argument. The governed host supplies its commissioning principal.
- Calendar fields minute/hour/day_of_month/month/day_of_week default to
  {"kind":"any"}; absent year remains absent. Compare canonical meaning while
  preserving explicit constraints and policies.
- Inventory and exact-ID readback are needed before creating or retrying after
  an unknown result. Labels do not grant ownership. A missing list entry alone
  does not settle an ambiguous create outcome.

Evidence:
- Callback registration is not schedule creation. Tool schemas are not grants.
  An agent-supplied schedule-shaped callback payload is not an authenticated
  native receipt. Native admission, occurrence completion and useful application
  work must be observed separately; do not replay side effects to obtain proof.
- Keep original operation, native ID and configuration across restart. Prove the
  persisted native schedule, actual delivery and useful stored result separately.
  Offline source and fixture checks cannot establish installed execution.

trigger.description: When the schedule fires. Uses internally tagged JSON with a "type" field. Three types: "once" fires at a single UTC timestamp. "interval" fires repeatedly every N seconds from a start time (optional end_at_utc). "calendar" fires on cron-style fields in a named IANA timezone. Examples: {"type":"once","due_at_utc":"2026-04-10T14:00:00Z"} | {"type":"interval","start_at_utc":"2026-04-10T14:00:00Z","every_seconds":60} | {"type":"calendar","timezone":"UTC","minute":{"kind":"values","values":[0]},"hour":{"kind":"values","values":[9,17]}}.

due_at_utc.description: Deliver once at this UTC timestamp.

end_at_utc.description: Optional final due time in UTC.

timezone.description: IANA timezone such as Europe/Stockholm or UTC.

day_of_week.description: Weekday values using the scheduler's cron-style domain: 0-6 and weekday names such as MON or FRI.

target.description: Where the schedule delivers. Uses target_kind to select session, identity, mob, or host_runnable. Host-runnable targets invoke an already registered host runnable by its published name, with optional opaque JSON params. The host owns runnable availability and execution; this target does not create a runnable or grant permission. Session targets: exact_session (deliver to a known session_id; fails if session is gone), resumable_session (deliver to a session_id that may be idle; runtime resumes it -- best for stable long-lived sessions), materialize_on_demand_session (create a new session on first fire using a "create" spec, then reuse it -- use when no session exists yet). Identity targets: resumable_identity (deliver to the current materialized session for a stable agent identity; host resolves at fire time). The identity string must be a form a schedule host on this surface can resolve, such as the mob-member form minted by the host; free-form strings are refused at create. Mob-member identity targets accept only prompt actions without session-only overrides (no system_prompt, skill_refs, or additional_instructions). Mob targets: member, flow, spawn_helper, fork_helper (deliver to a mob member or flow). Examples: schedule for yourself {"target_kind":"session","type":"current_session","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"Check in"}} | mob member {"target_kind":"identity","type":"resumable_identity","identity":"mob_member:{\"schema\":\"meerkat.schedule.mob_member_identity.v2\",\"mob_id\":\"ops\",\"member\":\"watcher\"}","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"Check in"}} | {"target_kind":"session","type":"materialize_on_demand_session","action":{"type":"prompt","prompt":"Run report"},"create":{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6"}}.

prompt.description: Either a plain text string or a list of multimodal content blocks.

system_prompt.description: Appended as an ordinary System message at this scheduled turn boundary.

bound_session_id.description: Only used by persisted materialize_on_demand_session schedules after the first materialization.

identity.description: Stable agent identity resolved by the schedule host at occurrence delivery time. Must be a host-recognized form (for example mob_member:{...} as minted by the host); arbitrary strings are refused at create because no host could ever deliver them.

prompt.description: Either a plain text string or a list of multimodal content blocks.

system_prompt.description: Appended as an ordinary System message at this scheduled turn boundary.

params.description: Raw JSON value for mob flow parameters.

content.description: Either a plain text string or a list of multimodal content blocks.

runnable.description: Published name of a host-registered runnable; empty or whitespace-only names are invalid.

params.description: Optional opaque JSON payload passed to the runnable. Omit when no payload is needed.

misfire_policy.description: What happens when the scheduler misses an occurrence's due time (e.g., downtime or lag). {"type":"skip"} (recommended): discard overdue occurrences after a ~30s grace window. {"type":"catch_up_within","window_seconds":N}: deliver the occurrence if it is overdue by less than N seconds, otherwise misfire. Use skip unless you specifically need late delivery.

overlap_policy.description: What happens when a new occurrence fires while a previous one is still running. "skip_if_running" (recommended): skip the new occurrence to prevent pile-up. "allow_concurrent": deliver both, allowing parallel execution. Use skip_if_running unless the target is designed for concurrent prompts.

missing_target_policy.description: What happens when the target session or mob does not exist at fire time. "mark_misfired" (recommended): record the occurrence as misfired so failures are visible. "skip": silently skip the occurrence. Use mark_misfired unless you expect transient target absence and do not want noise.
